claims.statement: Launch-time env-files are layered global → project so that the LAST assignment wins (podman --env-file is last-wins; the host twin applies the same order to a KEY->value map), and within one directory a `.env.schema` wins over a sibling `.env` while a bare `.env` is read literally with quotes/export prefixes stripped.

The host-env forward of CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is WITHHELD whenever any resolved env-file declares the variable — an explicit empty value is a declaration meaning OFF, not absence — because `podman run -e` beats `--env-file` and an unconditional forward once let a stale shell export outrank every declared source so a per-project token could never take effect (bd harnessed-36l).

`_env_files_value` computes the value a variable ends up with across the ordered env-files as the LAST declaration (empty string included, unreadable files skipped, None when never declared), matching how podman applies --env-file; answering from the first hit would let a global token mask a project-level `VAR=` written to disable it.

Presence checks must agree with value precedence: `_claude_oauth_token_configured` resolves every dir (global then project) and keeps the LAST declaration — empty meaning not configured — because returning True on the global hit left the container with no usable token AND no credential file, logged out with no recovery path from inside the pod (bd harnessed-7bk); varlock resolution is memoized so resolving every dir costs no extra subprocesses.

For an isolated_auth claude stack, `_strip_var_from_env_files` deletes the token variable from the generated env-file temps in place because `--env-file` is passed to podman unconditionally and a user-global declaration would walk straight past the other suppressions; this is safe only because every env-file path is a mode-0600 temp harnessed generated (a plain `.env` is copied, never handed to podman).

On the running container, recipe `env:` `-e` assignments go FIRST and harnessed-owned values later because podman applies `-e` left-to-right so the last wins and catalog-authored values must not clobber harness-owned ones; host mode mirrors this by applying `_recipe_env` to os.environ and then overwriting with the folder-env contract — reordering the pair silently inverts precedence between modes (caught merging harnessed-0tk.7 and harnessed-8px.2).

The install-script env contract wins in BOTH modes as inherited environment → recipe `env:` → harnessed-owned install vars applied LAST: container mode via `{**resolve_recipe_env(...), **install_env}` passed as inline `-e VAR=...` assignments that beat preceding image ENV lines, host mode via `env.update(recipe_env)` followed by `env.update(emit.install_env(...))` — asserted as order, not values (test_install_env_precedence), fixing the winner drift the harnessed-8px.2 merge exposed.

On host installs, the harness config-dir pinning (`_harness_config_env`) runs LAST so an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR from a parent stack's session cannot redirect an install into the wrong home — pinned rather than unset because unsetting would land writes in the user's real `~/.claude`; gsd-core's install.sh with an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR wrote 69 skills into an unrelated stack's home (bd harnessed-8px.26).

The host mise redirect clears as well as sets: `_apply_host_mise_env` runs after the `**os.environ` splat, actively removes only a harnessed-written stale MISE_STATE_DIR so an outer stack session's value cannot survive the merge, and `MISE_NPM_PACKAGE_MANAGER=pnpm` is placed after the splat so it wins as a default a user cannot usefully countermand (with `auto` the install fails).

Only the build-resolvable subset of recipe `env:` is baked as image ENV (emitted before the recipe's Dockerfile body; project-templated values are omitted rather than half-substituted), while the FULL resolved set is re-applied at launch on the container (-e) and the host (os.environ) so the running env is complete and identical across modes.

Within one stack, later recipes win on an `env:` clash: `_recipe_env` updates the map in recipe order, deliberately matching the Dockerfile layering (a later ENV overrides an earlier one), so stack recipe order is the load-bearing tie-breaker.

settings.json is merged, never copied, on relaunch: `_ensure_config_volume` copies the profile into the config volume on every launch but routes settings.json through `_merged_settings_text`, which deep-merges the installed volume file as base with the profile as overlay (profile wins on keys it defines, installer keys survive) — a plain copy dropped every install-written key on every relaunch after the first (bd harnessed-8px.19, 'ccstatusline statusLine gone on every restart').

The post-build settings merge treats the installer-written baked file as authoritative: `_merge_baked_settings` reads settings.json out of the config VOLUME first (the image read is only the fallback since `install:` moved off image layers, bd harnessed-8px.21.4) and runs unconditionally because the agent base image is an independent bake surface; `emit.merge_settings` then applies required.defaultMode with setdefault (floor, not override — a baked mode keeps it), unions the hatago grant into permissions.allow while stripping it from permissions.deny (required wins — hatago is the only MCP path), and carries every other baked key through verbatim.

Required hooks are merged into the baked settings with whole-entry union dedup (bd harnessed-8px.15) because the assemble-time floor is written from the same `required` dict the merge re-applies — appending without dedup duplicated every recipe hook so the agent ran each one twice per event; `warn_duplicate_hooks` remains as a detector that warns (never hard-fails) on identical (event, matcher, command) triples.

Absent is not empty on either settings read: `read_baked_settings` distinguishes an absent file (None, silent — keep the floor) from malformed JSON (None plus a warning — a recipe's bad file must not crash the build), and `_volume_read` maps a failed read to None, not "", because treating an unreadable volume as empty made the merge warn and keep the floor, reproducing the harnessed-8px.19 regression; absent correctly means 'copy the profile'.

`--fresh` is the one plain-copy case for settings.json: it discards the config volume (removed when the stack fingerprint moves, because composition is purely additive and a reused volume would keep a removed recipe's files forever), so there is nothing to preserve and the profile copy stands.

Host mode mirrors the settings merge twice: `_merge_host_claude_settings` merges the live `~/.claude/settings.json` into the profile and re-applies the required grants (dropping the host's host-absolute statusLine that cannot resolve in a container), then `_propagate_host_settings` writes the freshly computed profile over the live home carrying only keys the profile does not define — without the first, a host session ran on the bare assemble-time floor and a user's `auto` mode silently became `acceptEdits` (bd harnessed-8px.8); without propagating on every launch (bd harnessed-8px.18), host-side fixes and preference edits never reached the live config.

Catalog entries resolve across roots searched user overlay (~/.config/harnessed/catalog) first, shipped repo catalog second, and the generated root ($XDG_DATA_HOME/harnessed/generated) last and only when it exists: `find_in_catalog` returns the first existing candidate so the overlay wins on a name clash, `list_catalog` dedupes by name the same way, and the generated root is last so a machine-minted stack can never shadow an authored one.

Because the overlay's win is also a silent loss, the loader warns when a recipe resolves from the user overlay and shadows the repo copy — `load_stack_with_recipes` on the production path prints once per name which copy is used and which is shadowed (sessions had quietly assembled stale overlay content causing real regressions); only recipes warn, stacks/agents/services stay silent, and `default` is exempt as a documented blessed override.

`dynstack.mint` refuses a derived stack name that collides with an authored stack — the authored manifest would win resolution (generated root is last) while the generated one sat ignored, so `run` would silently execute something the user did not ask for (reported on PR #176); refuse rather than shadow.

Stack `extends:` merges on the RAW dict before field parsing: recipes/services/harnesses/ssh_keys UNION (parent entries first, deduped), every other declared field is a child-wins override with omitted keys inherited (declared values replace, they do not deep-merge), `name` is never inherited, `extends` is consumed, chains are allowed, and cycles are an error; the parent resolves against the child's own catalog root first so an overlay stack can extend a repo one.
Unknown stack top-level fields are rejected rather than ignored because tolerant parsing once let an `extends:` written before the feature existed look accepted while inheriting nothing for months.

`--extends` defaults to the literal name `default` on both run verbs, every dynamic stack mints `extends: default`, and with neither --stack nor --recipe the baseline itself is the stack that runs (a legitimate launch); `--no-extends` inherits from nothing so it requires at least one --recipe and is rejected otherwise.

The shipped `catalog/stacks/default` baseline is deliberately minimal and policy-free — one recipe, no services, no permissions/forwarding/isolation fields — because it is inherited by every dynamic stack on every install and a shipped policy would silently apply everywhere; a user replaces it wholesale by authoring ~/.config/harnessed/catalog/stacks/default/stack.yaml, which wins resolution on the name clash, and first run seeds the shipped default recipe into the user's overlay where it deliberately shadows the repo copy from then on.

When a directory mount and a file mount share a destination prefix, podman applies the more-specific destination: `_omp_mcp_seed_mount` mounts a per-instance mcp.json read-only over the shared `~/.omp/agent` bind mount so a stack's MCP servers reach omp without mutating the host file the dir mount shares.
